Like A Hurricane

hurricane600×400 47 KB

Type: Dangerous Event
Key Appearance: Covert Tactics (Vol. 3) #26, January 1987

Traits:

  • Roaring Wind d10
  • Flashing Lightning d8
  • Raining Bullets d8

GREEN
Minor Twists

  • Focused Gusts: It’s as though the wind hates you personally. Roll the environment dice and Hinder one hero with the Mid die.
  • The Red Wind: A group of terrorists emerges to attack! Roll the environment dice and create a number of d8 “Red Wind” minions equal to the Min die. They have +1 to Hinder.

Major Twist

  • Lightning Strike: The skies open up and the thunder rolls. Roll the environment dice and Attack a group of targets who are near each other with the Mid die.

YELLOW
Minor Twists

  • Shielding Winds: The hurricane seems to be supporting the villains! Roll the environment dice and Boost a villain target with the Max die.
  • The Cold Wind: One of Vortex’s true lieutenants emerges to fight. Create a d8 “Cold Wind” villain lieutenant.

Major Twist

  • Wind Generator: One of the wind generators kicks into high gear, offering a chance to track it down. Roll the environment dice. Hinder all heroes with the Mid die, then create the following challenge: Safely disable the generator. When the challenge is resolved, step down the environment’s Roaring Winds die one step.

RED
Minor Twists

  • Blast of Lightning: The hurricane’s power is getting more focused. Roll the environment dice and Attack one hero with the Max+Min dice.
  • Wall of Wind: The generators are increasingly protected as the storm worsens. Roll the environment dice and Hinder all heroes with the Max die.

Major Twist

  • Incoming Missile Strike: AEGIS has identified the generator location and is on its way. This is not a good thing. Advance the scene tracker.

Scenario Notes: This event typically includes a Doomsday Device, and uses the Epic scene tracker.

As the Iron Age dawned, a growing number of comics in the Venture setting focused on heroes getting caught between clearly villainous activity, and a government that was fearful, distrustful, or too quick on the draw. Covert Tactics served as the spearhead for these stories, able to both demonstrate the need for heroes and, through Madame Liberty’s cover identity with AEGIS, offer direct insight into how the government was (mis)handling situations.

This also offered a chance to revamp some classic villains, bringing them in line with the new, grittier comics era. One strong beneficiary of this work was Vortex. Freed of her initial origin as a Chinese communist agent, Vortex was reimagined as still being the result of Chinese government experimentation into creating superhumans, but one who went rogue almost immediately after her powers manifested, becoming a freelance terrorist, bodyguard, and trainer for other terrorist groups. Vortex considered herself the enemy of all hegemonic states, but with America in the ascendancy she considered them her primary threat. She believed that global cooperation was impossible; all nations would ultimately be at odds with each other, and only a world with no superpowers could survive. Any agents of an imperialist power were valid targets, and all citizens of imperialist powers were their agents.

Vortex’s first major foray in the Iron Age was the “Like a Hurricane” storyline. Working with a small terrorist cell that called themselves the Red Wind, and who wished to return the world to its agricultural roots, Vortex connected herself to a dangerously untested hurricane generator, using it to boost her powers to a point where she could wipe an entire city off the map. Her goal was to push AEGIS into launching a large-scale missile strike on the factories in Neulyon’s eastern districts, damaging American industry and fostering distrust of the American government in its people, and pinning the blame on her patsies without anyone learning that she was involved.

AEGIS became aware of the situation when one of their agents was killed by the Red Wind. When AEGIS sent their new Agent Apollo, Rick Wilson, to resolve the situation, Madame Liberty and Covert Tactics mobilized to protect him. They were fighting on a timer, because Vortex’s plan was working – AEGIS had mapped out the damage that the hurricane generator could do, and were preparing a large-scale missile strike to take the heavily-reinforced building down if the generator wasn’t shut down in time. Discovering Vortex’s involvement, Madame Liberty was able to disconnect her from the generator while her team dealt with the Red Wind, shutting down the operation with AEGIS’s jets already in the air.

The incident helped to cement Covert Tactics’ distrust of AEGIS, develop an ideology for Vortex that worked alongside her more common mercenary work without making her particularly sympathetic, and made it clear just how dangerous the new world order was becoming. The popularity of the comic led to the growth of AEGIS as an active threat rather than an obstacle, with readers agreeing that AEGIS’s willingness to kill thousands to ‘protect’ the rest of the city showing that they were one of the villains that needed to be dealt with.

Behind The Scenes:

My Iron Age environments are a little bit tilted towards 90s gonzo, but I wanted at least one setup for the early years of the Iron Age and how that grittiness was being applied, and Covert Tactics seemed like the right place for it. It’s also a good place for Vortex; we know that she’s a big enough deal to get a legacy character treatment in 2001, but I didn’t really know what she was up to in the 80s and 90s. I’d also made a comment about her claiming to fight for equality and raising her daughter that way, which wasn’t fully in line with “mercenary for hire”. So this rounds that storyline out.

This is not the first generated weather event I’ve written up. They’re useful things to have in the back pocket!

posts.cooked: That’s a good distinction. The pre-Code era could get away with quite a bit more, but 1967 really would have been an awkward point for a mainstream superhero setting. A coffeehouse or late-night diner might fit the period better while still giving the characters a regular gathering place

The Aurora Borealis

Aurora Borealis600×400 304 KB

Type: Heroic Location
Key Appearance: Celestial Travels #601, March 1989

Traits:

  • Nuclear Core d10
  • Esoteric Amenities d8
  • Aurora d8

GREEN
Minor Twists

  • Defensive Field: Aurora deploys internal force fields to protect the Travellers! Roll the environment dice and Defend each heroic target with the Min die.
  • Activate Internal Sensors: The systems are having trouble tracking intruders. Create a new challenge: Get the sensors working. Until the challenge is resolved, the GM does not need to reveal activity in any location that a hero is not in. When the challenge is resolved, create a +2 “Sensor Lock” bonus that can be used by any hero.

Major Twist

  • Gravity Glitch: The ship’s gravity flickers in a hyper-localized area. Roll the environment dice and Hinder one target with the Max die.

YELLOW
Minor Twists

  • Exploding Consoles: A set of consoles explodes as damage ripples through the ship. Roll the environment dice and Attack all targets in one location with the Mid die.
  • Blast Doors: Aurora seals all of the problems away where they can’t hurt anybody. Until the start of the next environment turn, anyone wanting to move between locations must succeed at an Overcome.

Major Twist

  • Direct Assistance: Aurora directly interfaces with one of the crew. Roll the environment dice and Boost one heroic target with the Max die. This bonus is persistent and exclusive.

RED
Minor Twists

  • Arsenal Breach: The intruders breach one of the Aurora Borealis’s armories. Roll the environment dice and Boost multiple villain targets with the Max die.
  • Reactor Breach: The Aurora Borealis’s nuclear reactor is going critical – if it isn’t fixed, it may have to be ejected! Create a new challenge: Stabilize the reactor.

Major Twist

  • Gravity Breach: The previous brief gravity problems just got a lot more severe. Roll the environment dice and Hinder using the Mid die. This penalty is persistent and exclusive and applies to anyone who can’t operate easily in zero gravity. Also Defend all targets on the ship with the Min die for as long as the penalty exists.

Neutrino’s iconic spaceship, the Aurora Borealis, underwent several revisions over the course of Celestial Travels in response to shifts in the comic’s tone and style. Initially designed to resemble a cylindrical three-prong rocket in the style of pulp spaceships of the time, drawn in a mixture of green and gold to reflect the patterns of its namesake, the rocket was deliberately designed as a tight one-man craft, with a cockpit, small eating area where Neutrino could visit with a guest of the week, and a sleeping area in the back near the engines. During the Dimensional Devastation event the Aurora Borealis was captured and then wrecked stopping the Empress of Ash, part of a plan to open room for a team of heroes to join Neutrino on his travels.

The revamped Aurora Borealis was the one that most comics fans thought of when they thought of Celestial Travels. Flat and sleek, with ‘solar sails’ on the sides and a shimmering cockpit in the back, the ship held enough room for a crew of six, although for most of the 1970s only three people occupied it for any length of time and Wavelength and Doctor Cosmos occupied the same crew cabin to ‘save space’. It also featured an integrated artificial intelligence called “Aurora” – although not technically sentient, Aurora had a rudimentary ability to respond to threats and anticipate the needs of the crew, and most of them often interacted with it like one would a particularly smart pet.

When the Celestial Travelers grew to five members after Peacemonger’s invasion, the first comics issue was dedicated to their ship and the complicated relationship of three people who had been journeying together for some time suddenly needing to open themselves to a new romantic couple joining the team, a pair who were still reeling from the dissolution of their own team and their need to not be on Earth for a while. Half-Life and Ember were grateful to join the Celestial Travelers; Half-Life in particular was glad to be with his old partner Wavelength again, and to help to recover his still-fragmented memories, and Ember was glad to have a chance to prove herself. Half of Celestial Travels #601 was dedicated to the five heroes working around each other, figuring out where they stood, and deciding whether their new arrangement was going to be temporary or ongoing.

The other half was about Subjugator and the Starbooters trying to hijack the ship, having carefully set up a team designed to hit Neutrino, Wavelength, and Reckoner where they were weakest.

The pirates overloaded Aurora, confusing the AI and shorting out the ship’s internal sensors, and then invaded armed with cosmic bafflers and nuclear-absorbing technology. Reckoner was still wrestling with her new powers and was quickly taken down, and Wavelength was caught mid-teleport and knocked out. Half-Life caught the raiders off-guard, but his nuclear powers were similar enough to Neutrino’s to be vulnerable – but Ember’s command of flame was not, and in fact the technology the Starbooters were using proved to be particularly vulnerable to overheating. Despite gravity failures, several failed attempts by Aurora to assist with the situation, and Subjugator’s raw power, the Starbooters were quickly forced back, their ship entering a warp path while damaged and vanishing into the depths of space.

The Celestial Travelers were quickly established after that. While they might bicker and need to figure out their space, they’d been through a confusing, complicated mess and come out the other side, and their further adventures across the Iron Age would reinforce their connections and gradually help them become a family.

Behind The Scenes:

Another one I’ve been planning for a while, to the point that I barely used any randomizers this time. The Celestial Travelers are a group that really need to have some more detail filled in, and a chance to have the “inside of the ship” environment seemed too good to pass up!

“Gah! My spleen is suddenly experiencing 5 gees! How did that happen?”

I blame Doctor Demiurge. IYKYK.

FrivYeti:

Exploding Consoles: A set of consoles explodes as damage ripples through the ship. Roll the environment dice and Attack all targets in one location with the Mid die.

“Dammit, who stored all these pyrotechnics in there?”

I blame Doctor Demiurge.

FrivYeti:

Arsenal Breach: The intruders breach one of the Aurora Borealis’s armories. Roll the environment dice and Boost multiple villain targets with the Max die.

“We have multiple armories?”

I blame Doctor Demiurge. And yet, he’s still storing overflow explosives in our control panels.

Wait, does Doctor Demiurge even exist on this universe? Eh, he’s probably omniversal.

Pretty hero-friendly environment overall, but of course all their stuff is on board so there’s some added stakes if they wind up having to eject their reactor or get taken over by space pirates or something.

Very minor proofing note: The Red Reactor Breach twist didn’t get bolded properly.

When did Hero Forge start including options for building spacecaft? Are their seplljammers too? I may have to take another look at the site.

Do they do mecha by any chance? The first place that starts offering a way to do suitable custom mechs is going to see a bajillion orders from the Lancer community, but getting the design style right would be tricky.

posts.cooked:
HeroForge doesn’t have options for building spacecraft, I’m just testing out how ridiculous I can get with kitbashing. The answer is pretty ridiculous if you’re willing to take the time.

This one uses a stretched out and squished cylinder as the base, with a jetpack layered into it to create the side wings and a different jetpack stretched out in the back for engines, and then a pair of rayguns pressed in for weapons, a version of the orb that Doctor Cosmos holds for the cockpit, and a metal backpack on the front giving it a front bulk feel.

(Doctor Demiurge doesn’t exist in Venture; I would want CKirby’s permission first and they haven’t been around in over a year. Charlie Foxtrot and the clone soldier species could show up as a Diamond Age thing, I can definitely see them appearing there as one of the other Celestial Traveler teams that shows up periodically, and I’d be happy for Phade to be on that team too with your permission.)

FrivYeti:

Exploding Consoles: A set of consoles explodes as damage ripples through the ship. Roll the environment dice and Attack all targets in one location with the Mid die.

Looks like whoever built the ship went to the Starfleet School of Engineering.

It certainly worked out well. Could they theoretically print that out for you? Or is there some kind of vetting process where some extreme custom jobs fail to pass the “can exist as physical object” and get rejected for that service?

No sense in having all those d10s in Stealth, Invisibility, Teleportation, and Principle of Stealth to go with them if you’re just going to let yourself get captured - or even noticed when you don’t feel like it.

posts.name: FrivYeti
posts.cooked:
Chief_Lackey_Rich:

It certainly worked out well. Could they theoretically print that out for you? Or is there some kind of vetting process where some extreme custom jobs fail to pass the “can exist as physical object” and get rejected for that service?

My understanding is that HeroForge kitbashing runs on a “at your own risk” model. If you request it, they’ll run the print, and if it doesn’t print successfully because of something you kitbashed they’ll send you the unsuccessful print. I don’t think they have a particular verification system, you just get a junk piece (there’s a particular warning about attaching large items to small hands.)

posts.name: Chief Lackey Rich
posts.cooked:
Interesting. Even a badly flawed attempt at a print could be useful for physical kitbashing, but I suppose it wouldn’t be a very economical way to fuel that mill.

Why am I not surprised they get enough attempts at adding comically-oversized weapons to figs that it merits a specific warning? Buster swords, hammers with heads big enough to be anvils instead, and ridiculously oversized 90s Image firearms must be irresistible to many gamers.

Welp.

As per Christopher’s announcement, this will be my final post over here on the GTG forums. It has been a great time, and I hope that I’ve brought a bit of joy.

If you’d like to continue following the progress of Venture Comics, you can find the companion thread over here on RPG.net. Those of you who aren’t already chatting over there (waving to Rich) might think of making an account and following along.

Otherwise, I’ll still be assembling these into full PDF volumes over on my Itch page, which is linked at the top of this thread, and I’ll still be linking them on the fan Realm of Discord.

It’s been a blast. Thanks for following along. The only thing left to do is… crash this thread into the sea!!!

Neo-Avalon

Neo-Avalon600×400 217 KB

Type: Unique
Key Appearance: Knightgrave Annual #3, July 1990

Traits:

  • Blood-Drive Engine d10
  • Gas-Line Propellers d8
  • Deadly Gusts d8

GREEN
Minor Twists

  • Fusion Burst: Neo-Avalon rains fire down on the heroes. Roll the environment dice and Attack any hero who hasn’t made it onboard with the Min die.
  • Catalyst Knights: Roll the environment dice and create a number of d8 “Bloodsworn Knight” minions equal to the Min die. When one is defeated, roll its status die and Boost another minion with the result.

Major Twist

  • Strain Appears: Neo-Avalon is less invincible than it appears. Now and at the start of each turn, roll a and create the following challenge:
    • 1-3: Steal blood from the Blood-Drive Engine to reduce the Blood-Drive Engine die by one step.
    • 4-6: Shatter the gas lines across the ship to reduce the Gas-Line Propellers die by one step.

YELLOW
Minor Twists

  • Gas Rupture: A gas line bursts over someone. Roll the environment dice and Attack a target with the Mid die. Hinder them with the Min die.
  • Hostages! X-Calibre’s men return with civilian hostages. Create the following challenge: Save the hostages before they’re killed! If the scene tracker reaches Red before the challenge is solved, kill the hostages and increase the Blood-Drive Engine die by one step.

Major Twist

  • Galahad: X-Calibre’s merciless second-in-command is on the scene. Create a d8 “Galahad” lieutenant. When he Boosts, he may target up to three minions. He may immediately take a Boost action.

RED
Minor Twists

  • Blood Magic: The engine is roaring out of control. Roll the environment dice and Attack a target with the Mid die. Boost the same target with the Min die. The bonus is persistent and exclusive.
  • Rampaging Knights : The Bloodsworn are growing stronger. Create (H) d10 “Bloodsworn Marauder” minions. When one of them dies, step up the others’ status dice once.

Major Twist

  • Ramming Speed: It may be too late. Remove all “Strain Appears” challenges currently in play. Roll a for each challenge removed and Attack all targets aboard Neo-Avalon with the total result.

Scenario Note: If any environment die drops below d4, Neo-Avalon crashes into the English Channel at the start of the next environment turn, saving the city and posing a devastating threat to anyone still on board.

By the early 1990s, Venture was using its ‘Annual’ issues primarily for big summer and winter crossover events. Most of these events featured three or four annual issues, along with one or two standard issues or one-shots linked to the main event taking place. In the summer of 1990, the decision was made for the main annual crossover to be between Knightgrave and the Champions of Truth. Greenheart was in Japan on her ill-considered ‘ninja’ arc, although she was returning to the Champions periodically for their own battles, and it seemed like a good time for a few of the Champions to come to England for a devastating battle against a foe that had lost some of his shine over the past few years.

X-Caliber had become a bit of a joke in the late 1980s; after a strong start in the first two years of Knightgrave, he’d faded into the background as Knightgrave dealt with the Ravenmaster, Sleight, and the six demon princes seeking Merlin’s head. His most recent appearance, the year before, had featured an attempt to join forces with the Dread Dynasty that ended with him mocked and spurned by the power-supremacist aristocrats. In the hopes of revitalizing the villain and moving him back into position as Knightgrave’s greatest enemy, the Venture editorial room collaborated on a new attempt to bring ruin to England.

The story kicked off in Knightgrave Annual #3, with Baron Carmichael discovering the grave of Mordred Pendragon. His men were able to unearth remnants of Mordred’s endless battles during his centuries of death, coalescing into blood crystals that they were able to use to exsanguinate captive civilians. The resulting crystals held phenomenal power, and X-Caliber was able to use them to construct his ultimate flying fortress, Neo-Avalon! Powered by ancient blood magic mixed with modern technology, the fortress was able to project an energy shield that guarded it from missiles and assault. With his forces arrayed behind him, X-Caliber flew Neo-Avalon into the heart of London, threatening to rain death upon the city unless the House of Windsor abdicated and declared him the rightful King of England. His knights began kidnapping government officials and civil servants, holding them as hostages that could be used to bolster the blood crystals powering his ship and his followers.

Knightgrave tried to handle Neo-Avalon himself, but the fortress’s magic was turned on him, weakening his own blood magic and nearly ending his immortal life. X-Caliber stabbed him through the heart and threw him from the platform to drown in the Thames. At the last moment, Knightgrave was rescued by Wonderer, Penitent, and Skybreaker, who had arrived in the nick of time to deal with what was rapidly becoming an international incident.

Over the course of Skybreaker Annual #18 and Champions of Truth Annual #12, the four heroes set themselves against Neo-Avalon, using a mixture of force, guile, and persuasion to find and turn the members of Carmichael’s household who were horrified at the murders taking place against him, weaken the blood-driven engine, and ultimately direct the entire fortress into the English Channel. The final battle was fierce, with Knightgrave returning the blade Carmichael had driven into him back into X-Caliber’s chest. The fortress sank, and the synthesized blood crystals were lost, preventing another from being created.

Carmichael survived, of course. He successfully argued in court that he had been corrupted by exposure to an undead knight, and that Mordred Pendragon had been the one truly responsible for Neo-Avalon. Most people didn’t believe him, but just enough did to keep Knightgrave in an uncomfortable position with the law and to keep X-Caliber out of jail. He would go on to be a persistent thorn in Knightgrave’s side, wielding power and the law against him.

Behind The Scenes:

Now we’re getting extreme! Stolen blood magic, draining people of their blood to power a giant flying fortress, somehow blaming the heroes for it at the end and getting off scot-free. That’s the nineties, baby! Weirdly appropriate for a final post over here.

In all seriousness, I do love this story as a summer annual. It makes no sense. It’s absolutely silly. It’s great.
